title: Product Comparison Videos for Clearer Choices | AIVideosUGC
description: Show shoppers the difference between your colors, sizes, or sets. One photo of both options becomes a comparison clip for listings, YouTube Shorts and paid ads.
h1: Make a Product Comparison Video Shoppers Can Judge
lead: A product comparison video lets shoppers judge two options in one look, when both sit in a single photo. Choose a side-by-side layout from the wall and use a picture that already holds the pair.
steps_h2: How to Make a Product Comparison Video in 3 Simple Steps
steps_lead: One shared frame lets shoppers judge the small and large canisters. Two photos shot on different days make a weak comparison.

steps.d: Show the small and large gray canisters together in one photo. Your chosen layout supplies the frame.
The small canister suits a shelf. The large one holds more, so say that in plain words.
A tall clip can linger on the larger canister. A square still can sit on the product page.

faq.q: What is a product comparison template?
faq.a: A product comparison template is a ready-made layout that holds two choices in one view. A home shop can keep the small canister and the large canister side by side, at a scale a shopper can judge.

faq.q: How does a comparison template become a video?
faq.a: Place the pair photo in the layout, write how the two canisters differ, and export a square for the listing. A shopper can point at one option without guessing.

faq.q: Why use this instead of hiring someone to film both options?
faq.a: You can publish the comparison before a filming day opens up. The pair photo is already in the listing, so the ad does not sit behind that search.

faq.q: Who should use a comparison template?
faq.a: Owners, marketers, and founders who sell two close choices and have to explain them in one breath. The person writing the line is often the shop owner.

faq.q: Can someone new to video make one?
faq.a: Yes. Someone who has never cut a timeline can still make it. They pick the side-by-side layout. The photo of both items does the arranging.

faq.q: Which products can I compare with this template?
faq.a: Any pair a shopper has to weigh can use it, such as a small canister beside a large one. Both sizes have to be in that one photo. A hero shot of a single item is the wrong start.

faq.q: Can I use my own pair photo, a clip, and a logo?
faq.a: Yes. A pair photo that already includes the logo is the right start. A short clip of the two products being set down can be the motion.

faq.q: Which placements and sizes fit a comparison?
faq.a: YouTube, a Facebook Story, the product page, and a banner each have a frame. YouTube is comfortable at 16:9. A Facebook Story wants 9:16 at 6 or 10 seconds. The product page can take 1:1, and 4:3 or 3:4 covers a banner. 15 and 30 seconds are there when the difference needs more time.

faq.q: Do I need a paid plan to use a template?
faq.a: Yes. Starter is $24.50 a month with 200 credits, Pro is $35 with 300, and Premium is $63 with 600. A photo spends 24 credits. A 6, 10, 15, or 30 second clip spends 24, 40, 60, or 120 credits. The total shows before the run, and a failed run gives those credits back.

faq.q: Can I run the comparison in ads and client work?
faq.a: Yes. Run the pair as a paid ad and place the same file on the product page, including work for a client. The download has no watermark.

faq.q: What does a side-by-side template already include?
faq.a: The layout already chooses which option sits on the left and when the difference is spoken. You write how the two canisters differ. You do not invent the shot list.

steps.sourceTitle: Two Sizes of a Matte Storage Canister
steps.sourceHint: Keep the small and large slate-gray canisters, rounded lids and blank surfaces fully visible.
steps.prompt: An adult raises a small and a large gray canister to the same height.

reviews.h2: How Shops Use a Comparison Video
reviews.lead: Both options stay in one picture. A voice, a script, or an on-screen person can name the difference.

items.d: A home shop puts the small bottle next to the large one, then checks both stay visible.
A drinkware shop starts from one photo of charcoal and cream tumblers and makes the comparison clip from it.
An apparel shop has an AI actor turn navy and rust beanies so the knit difference is easy to see.
A bag shop opens two canvas packs together and shortens the spoken line in the built-in editor.
A kitchen shop shows a two-piece canister set, then a voice in another language for a second market.
A storage shop places short and tall bins in one scene and edits the script on the same page.
A bedding shop uses an AI actor to hold two pillow sizes at the same distance.
A tool shop uploads one photo of two handle finishes and skips a new lighting setup.
A furniture shop pastes the product link for a narrow shelf and a wide shelf, then makes a second version.
A pet shop types the two bowl sizes and checks the clip before it goes on the listing.

more_sections.lead: Voice, a script, and publishing stay beside the layout, so the comparison is finished in one place.

items.d: A stock voice, or a clone from a short sample, can name the difference out loud.
You can edit any line so it says how the two options differ. Begin with a note or the listing link.

items.t: An AI Avatar Points It Out
items.d: An AI avatar can gesture at either option, so you do not film a presenter. Drop in B-roll of each product when the choice needs a closer view.
Paste the product page for a first script. Your own software can also send the pair photo through the API.
Buyers in France can hear the small and large canisters named in French. The picture of the pair stays. The captions can move with that voice.

Another version for a different buyer comes from the same photo, so you can test two hooks. Send it to YouTube, TikTok, Instagram, or Facebook from a connected account, or download it and post on your own.
